newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Economists pick NZ core inflation at 2.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: Economists pick NZ core inflation at 2.00 pct.

text.p: A group of four bank economists polled by Reuters estimated on Tuesday that underlying inflation in the year to March 1997 would be 2.00 percent and up 0.2 percent for the quarter.
They based their estimate on figures released by Statistics New Zealand on Tuesday showing the Consumer Price Index fell 0.3 percent in the March quarter and rose by 1.8 percent in the March year.
However, the official statistics were strongly influenced by a 5.4 percent drop in credit services in the quarter caused by falling mortgage rates.
The Reserve Bank is due to release its own calculation of underlying inflation later this morning. This is a separate process to Statistics New Zealand's production of headline inflation data.
